A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DataRater: Meta-Learned Dataset Curation. Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the retained results table and expanded Appendix A.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, compute savings, downstream evaluations, filtering sensitivity analyses, and qualitative examples in Figures 1–9 and Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds perplexity-filter comparisons, meta-training diagnostics, and statistical analyses of learned scores in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 2 corrects the stated filtering rules: the oversampled batch size changes from N*rho/(1-rho) to N/(1-rho), and pointwise acceptance gains a binomial coefficient. These are limited corrections to the specified curation procedure; the architecture, meta-objective, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: The Pile, C4/noclean, and C4 remain the training corpora, with the same validation, Wikipedia, and five downstream evaluations. The new comparisons and diagnostics use existing coverage. Corrupted-data examples and conversational fine-tuning extensions already appear in v1.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates filtering primarily against unfiltered training. v2 adds three evaluated perplexity filters adapted from Ankner et al. (2025): PPLX (Top), PPLX (Mid), and PPLX (Bot) in Figure 10, followed by detailed comparisons with PPLX (Mid) in Figure 11. This substantially expands the competing filtering methods.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds a dedicated comparison using 150M inner, scorer, and evaluation models, distinct from the main results' 400M inner models. Selected discard fractions are 90% for PPLX (Mid) and 75%/50%/25% for DataRater across the three corpora. New diagnostics use 25,600 Pile sequences. Separately, the reported cosine weight-decay schedule becomes cosine learning-rate decay, without establishing that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained scale, discard-fraction, and checkpoint analyses, v2 adds filtering sensitivity comparisons with perplexity methods, per-model meta-update norm traces, checkpoint score correlations, and heuristic correlation/OLS/Lasso analyses. Figures 10 and 12–15 substantially expand evidence about filtering behavior, stability, and what the scores capture.

E5.justification: v2 adds 10-fold cross-validation repeated five times for the Lasso analysis. This is a new statistical estimation procedure, not evidence of five repeated language-model training runs. Figure 9's existing 95% confidence intervals are retained; the new filtering comparisons do not add uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Original Figures 1–9 and the numerical contents of v1 Table 1, now v2 Table 2, are retained. New Figure 11 reports DataRater best in 16 of 21 cases, PPLX (Mid) in four, and unfiltered training in one. New analyses report OLS R2=0.766, Lasso R2=0.753, and late-checkpoint score correlations above 0.95. These are additional findings, not improvements to the original same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Section 2 inserts the missing binomial factor C(B-1,s) into the pointwise acceptance probability and corrects the oversampling expression. These repair mathematical statements underlying filtering. The main bilevel formulation and Appendix B's noise-based reasoning remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain meta-learned data valuation, compute savings up to 46.6%, and generalization across 50M–1B evaluation models. Explicitly describing value as relative to the meta-objective restates a dependence already established in v1's formulation and limitations; the central scientific claims remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking scores mainly to document count, length, and non-alphanumeric content, and suggests unexplained regression variance may reflect patterns beyond the tested heuristics. It also explains population resets as promoting generalization across training stages. These extend the existing interpretation, while Appendix C's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies MixFlow-MG rematerialisation and saved inner gradients, clarifies FLOP accounting including filtering and oversampling, and documents the new analysis through heuristic definitions in Table 1, DataTrove provenance, feature normalization, and regularization settings. The existing hardware and training budgets are retained; no new DataRater code or dataset release is announced.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ankner et al. for perplexity filtering, Guo et al. for semi-supervised bilevel weighting, Li and Gong for multilingual reweighting, and the DeepMind JAX ecosystem reference. These modestly broaden positioning and attribution. The MixFlow-MG publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, section order, and most existing prose are retained. v2 makes targeted implementation and related-work rewrites, adds explanatory paragraphs and named topics within Appendix A, updates cross-references, and expands acknowledgements. This is a localized narrative expansion rather than extensive restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds six substantive displays: filtering comparisons, update-norm traces, two correlation heatmaps, and regression coefficients in Figures 10–15, plus a heuristic-definition table. Existing Figures 1–9 are retained; the original performance table is relocated and renumbered as Table 2. The appendix's visual evidence is substantially expanded.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important weakness in v1: the absence of an evaluated alternative filtering method. The controlled perplexity comparisons, stability diagnostics, and score analyses substantially strengthen the empirical assessment, while corrected filtering formulas and added implementation details improve correctness and reproducibility. The new comparisons still lack uncertainty estimates, and regression residuals do not establish that unexplained patterns are valuable, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantive gains.
